Let me break it down real simple how the two different cards work:

  1. Regular card, no chip - Your ENTIRE credit card number and expiration are stored in that magnetic strip in data form that never changes. You skim the strip, you can copy the data on a dummy card and the machine doesn't know the difference because the information never changes. So you swipe, and the machine (and the skimmer) sees "10101010", the guy who owns the skimmer copies that onto some other card, and now anytime he swipes that card, regardless of what numbers are printed on the front, the machine will see "10101010" and think it's your card. This is why it's really easy to steal normal cards.

  2. Chip card. - The machine communicates with the chip in your card directly, the chip offers up a one-time transaction code, makes sure the code that the machine offers is valid, and then processes the rest of the transaction. That code is worthless once the transaction is over so even if someone managed to skim the data from the transaction, they could literally do nothing with it. There is no feasible way for someone to skim your card information from a chipped transaction. This makes it astronomically harder to steal your credit card information or load stolen information onto dummy cards .
